findings.title: A failed test run can report a pass
findings.description: `unseen.sh` discards the Docker command’s status and returns success whenever it finds two score lines and zero parsed wrong values. The harness prints those scores before its final checks, so a later unexpected test failure can still leave the script reporting exit code 0.

findings.title: Engine changes can alter their own check
findings.description: `ci/guard.sh` does not classify the new checking script or checksum file as measuring files. A pull request can therefore change `src/` and weaken this check in the same change without triggering the guard that rejects joint engine-and-measure changes.

findings.title: Checking failures reveals unseen queries
findings.description: `SKILL.md` step 5 tells the agent to open the full output file, which contains the SQL and expected values for failing unseen records. When an engine returns a wrong value, the same agent asked to diagnose the failure sees material the skill says coding agents must never see.

findings.title: Custom paths can expose unseen files
findings.description: `unseen.sh` compares the unnormalized data path with the canonical repository path before accepting it. An absolute path containing `..` that resolves inside the checkout bypasses the check, allowing the downloaded tests and query-bearing run output to be written into the repository.

findings.title: An interrupted download blocks later runs
findings.description: `unseen.sh` downloads directly to the final filename and retries only when that file is absent. If a download leaves a partial file, later invocations skip the download and repeatedly fail checksum verification instead of recovering.

findings.title: Concurrent checks overwrite evidence
findings.description: `unseen.sh` names output files using a timestamp with only one-second precision. Two checks started during the same second use the same path and truncate or intermingle their output, so the saved evidence and parsed result need not belong to one run.
